dedupe_keys.name: testing the public s response to severe flood warnings using simulated cell broadcast smith grant and thomas natural hazards 2022

description: This open access study tested how people respond to cell broadcast messages that warn of floods of varying certainty, severity and urgency. European governments had to implement a public alerting system for mobile phone users by June 2022, and cell broadcast, used in several countries, had not yet been introduced in the UK. Using a mixed-methods approach with semi-structured questions and focus groups, the researchers assessed the perceptions of 80 workshop participants who received simulated emergency alerts on pre-prepared handsets. The results suggest emergency alerting is welcomed, but messages must be accurate and verifiable, address accessibility, and state location clearly; used without over-alerting and specifying urgency, certainty, severity and location, cell broadcast could upgrade UK flood warnings. Producer: Kate R. Smith, Silvia Grant and Robert E. Thomas, published in Natural Hazards, 16 February 2022 (volume 112). Coverage: UK workshops with 80 participants. Access: the article page blocked the cloud session, so the abstract and licence were taken from OpenAlex by DOI and the PMC page header. Licence and cost: free under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: no participant data release was confirmed and a workshop sample is not representative. Simulation uses: the response findings give behavioural assumptions for emergency-response and agent-based warning models. Related record: the US nationwide alert test of 2023 (case_study-us-nationwide-alert-test-2023).
